tooling.message:
feat(tooling): package @lernapps/tooling with the CLI lernapps, vite-plus, hooks and check in CI

## Intent

The tooling is built with the conventions it gives apps before anything is built on it (#10): one package installed from git, strict TypeScript, vite-plus as the toolchain, git hooks that enforce, and CI that runs exactly what the hooks run.

## Key changes

- The repo root is the package @lernapps/tooling; the CLI lernapps is built into dist/ on install, since Node does not strip types under node_modules.
- lernapps check: --pre-commit runs format, lint and type check, --pre-push runs tests and the package build; no flag or both flags run both.
- vite-plus hooks: pre-commit formats the staged files and runs the fast part; pre-push runs the rest. The new workflow check.yml runs both parts.
- Strict tsconfig, lint forbids any, a test forbids JavaScript sources; the review summary script is migrated to TypeScript.
- End-to-end tests on a fresh clone: a planted type error, lint error or failing test turns hooks and CI red; an install from git provides lernapps.
- The org preset groups vite-plus with its Vite core, which an npm override installs.
- README and plan (KD-21) describe the package, the hooks, the test approach and the commit format.

## Dependencies and side effects

- npm ci now also builds dist/ and sets the hooks path in the clone.
- Every repo that uses the org preset gets one grouped update for vite-plus and its core.

tooling.message:
feat(guidance): AGENTS.md, the plan template, its front matter schema and the skill lernapps-app

## Intent

Any assistant should follow the EPCC workflow from plain text (#14): keep a plan, follow its phases, stop at the creator's checkpoints and load the skills.

## Key changes

- AGENTS.md (at most 350 words, loaded in every turn) makes the assistant keep .vibe/plan.md from the template, work only in the phase the front matter names, stop at the checkpoints (confirm the plan, publish, list), never bypass a hook and fill in the retrospective.
- The plan template has Explore, Plan, Code and Commit with comments that guide the assistant; Explore fetches the published entry schema instead of repeating its fields; the retrospective has fixed headings.
- The front matter has a versioned JSON Schema: archetype, phase and prePushFailures; from phase plan on, archetype is required; unknown keys are rejected.
- The skill lernapps-app holds the workflow and the general rules; the package exports the guidance files.
- Contract tests read the real files as a consumer does, with a filled plan and four broken fixtures.
- The tests drop inherited GIT_* variables, so a run from a worktree's pre-push hook no longer acts on the repo being pushed.

tooling.message:
feat(rules): rule ids, the id test, the first listing and site rules, the rule page

## Intent

The rules live in their artifacts; they should still form one catalog (#11): one way to declare or implement a rule id per artifact kind, a test that fails on duplicates or missing links, the first rules, and a page that lists them.

## Key changes

- A rule is declared once by a rule block (id, scope, severity, enforcement) under the heading that explains it, in a skill or in the review rubric.
- Lint rules and checks carry only the id and the link to the rule's entry on the rule page; ids are unique per kind.
- The id test runs in lernapps check; the build renders the rule page at /tooling/rules/.
- The first rules of scope listing and site.
- The plan marks steps 2 and 5 as completed, with the deviations agreed in step 2.
